clue.text: Type of book that's difficult to finance

blocks.note: a hard task is a difficult one
to back a venture is to put money into it

explanation.surface: A grumble that one kind of book is hard to get funded.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardback is a book bound in stiff covers, as opposed to a paperback edition.

clue.text: He entertains a lot of people

blocks.note: first meaning: the man who receives and looks after guests
second meaning: a great crowd or multitude

explanation.surface: A generous party-giver who has many guests round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one sentence it describes a sociable man; split it and each half is a separate sense of the same short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the person who receives guests and a large number, as in a host of angels.

clue.text: Conclusion of those supporting free travel?

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, so only the end is kept
in a down clue a piece that supports another sits beneath it, so it is written after

blocks.note: to rid someone of a burden is to free them
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Asks whether free bus travel is the end result of a campaign by its supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'supporting' is about position in the grid, not backing a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride is a journey in a vehicle or on horseback, and as a verb it means to travel that way.

clue.text: Coming through arch, Nutmeg will wave

indicators.note: something coming through a structure is inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Nutmeg is the setter, who would say I'LL for 'I will'
a bow is a curved arch shape

explanation.surface: The setter promises to wave as she passes under an archway.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym stands for the first person, so 'Nutmeg will' becomes I'LL, placed inside BOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A billow is a great swelling wave of the sea, and billowing cloth moves in waves.

clue.text: Snooty prisoner sent down?

blocks.note: a con is a convict
going down, read literally rather than as being jailed

explanation.surface: A haughty convict who has just been jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent down' is British slang for being sent to prison, which fits the prisoner; here it simply means going downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Being condescending means talking down to others with an air of superiority, which is snooty behaviour.

clue.text: Trap Scotsman returning computer peripheral

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: a spider's web is a trap
Mac is a crossword name for a Scot, from the surname prefix

explanation.surface: Someone catching a Scot coming back home, oddly mixed with computer kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A webcam is a small video camera plugged into a computer, a typical add-on device.

clue.text: Rising church still full of enthusiasm

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
static means not moving

explanation.surface: A congregation getting to its feet, motionless yet bursting with fervour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic describes someone overwhelmed with joy and delight, brimming with excited feeling.

clue.text: Crosses bustling circus, avoiding small holes

indicators.note: bustling suggests hurried jostling movement, so these letters get jumbled
avoiding something means leaving it out, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small
being in a hole or a fix both mean being in trouble

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying across a busy circus ground while dodging small pits.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the S from CIRCUS before shuffling. 'Holes' are tight spots, like fixes, not gaps in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A crucifix is a cross bearing the figure of Christ, so the plural matches a noun meaning crosses.

clue.text: Island's foolhardy commanders on wheels

blocks.note: a mad scheme is a reckless one
an aga is an Ottoman commander or official
wheels is slang for a car

explanation.surface: An island's reckless military leaders riding about in vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay. AGA is a Turkish title for a military chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Madagascar is the large island nation off the south-east coast of Africa.

clue.text: Group of players with wrinkles removed from the limelight

blocks.note: a team is a side
a wrinkled face is lined

explanation.surface: Ageing team members being dropped from the spotlight.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sidelined means being pushed out of an active or prominent role, out of public attention.

clue.text: Doctor insured to accommodate particular health worker

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters get rearranged
accommodating something means making room for it inside, so another piece goes in

blocks.note: taken as written
a particular, fussy person is strict about details

explanation.surface: A medic covered by insurance housing a fussy community carer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a medical person, fitting the health theme, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A district nurse is a British nurse who visits patients at home within a local area, a community health worker.

clue.text: Safe stretch of water, that's what we hear

blocks.note: first meaning: secure, in good condition
second meaning: a narrow inlet or channel of the sea
third meaning: anything audible

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one word, as in safe and sound, Plymouth Sound, and a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means healthy or secure, names a sea channel, and is the general term for anything heard.

clue.text: Joining forces, Queen stops internees legging it

indicators.note: something that stops a gap plugs it, so it sits inside the other piece

blocks.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina
POWs are prisoners of war
haring is running fast like a hare

explanation.surface: The monarch halts a breakout of prisoners as they make a run for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stops' reads as halting an escape, but it means plugging a gap. 'Legging it' is British slang for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: Power-sharing is an arrangement where rival parties govern together, a joining of forces in government.

clue.text: Last of minor repairs to broken hospital equipment

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept
something broken is in pieces that can be put back in another order

blocks.note: final letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: The final small fix on some broken hospital machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A respirator is a machine that helps a patient breathe, standard kit in an intensive care ward.

clue.text: Request to screenwriter to submit work, as afterthought?

definitions.text: Request to screenwriter to submit work

blocks.clueFragment: Request to screenwriter to submit work
blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: an order to send off the screenplay
second meaning: a note added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A producer chasing a writer for the screenplay as a last-minute thought.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words it is an instruction to mail the screenplay; whole, it is the addition below a signature.
explanation.definitionFit: A PS is a note added after the signature of a letter, literally something written after the main text.

clue.text: Ancient God's aching back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: sore muscles ache

explanation.surface: An old deity complaining of a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aching back' looks like a single ailment, but back is the instruction to read the word in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros was the Greek god of love, a deity of classical antiquity.

clue.text: Shortages briefly alarm conurbations

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to scare is to alarm
a conurbation is a large urban area

explanation.surface: Supply shortfalls causing brief panic in big towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcities are situations where something is in short supply, so they are shortages.

clue.text: Picture showing erection of bridges stolen

indicators.note: erecting something stands it upright, and in a down clue going upward reverses the letters

blocks.note: a bridge spans a river
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A photo of the construction of some bridges, with something stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quick informal photograph, a kind of picture.

clue.text: Pretend to stage part of play?

blocks.note: first meaning: to feign feelings or behaviour
second meaning, read literally: to mount one section of a drama

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for faking it is also, word for word, what a theatre company does with one division of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts on an act is feigning, behaving falsely to create an impression.

clue.text: Very large component of management retiring

indicators.note: a component is a part, so the letters lie within the next word
retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the letters run from right to left

blocks.note: letters inside the word

explanation.surface: A huge part of the bosses is stepping down.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal for enormous, from the Greek prefix meaning great.

clue.text: Like Greek character about to have a dream

blocks.note: as means in the manner of
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
re means concerning

explanation.surface: Someone resembling a figure from Greek drama who is on the point of dreaming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as a single phrase meaning 'on the point of', but 'about' is one piece and 'to' merely joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to set one's hopes on an ambition, like Martin Luther King having a dream.

clue.text: Worker at counter notes price — it's appalling

indicators.note: something appalling is in a terrible state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shop assistant spots a shocking price tag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' splits: IT joins the fodder and the 's is 'is', the link to the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptionist greets visitors and deals with enquiries at a front desk, a counter in a hotel or office.

clue.text: PM's spoken of "complex network, difficult to leave"

indicators.note: something spoken of is said out loud, so we go by how the word sounds

blocks.note: Theresa May was a British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A prime minister's remark about a tangled system that is hard to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is Prime Minister; Theresa May led the UK government, and her possessive sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A maze is a confusing network of paths designed so it is hard to find the way out.

clue.text: Proceeded north in rainy season

indicators.note: one thing being in another places it within, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for north
the wet is the tropical rainy season

explanation.surface: Someone travelled northwards during the monsoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Went is the past tense of go, so it means moved forward or proceeded.

clue.text: A bit of leg tasting strong after last of breast

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept
after says this piece follows the next one in the answer

blocks.note: final letter of the word
game that is high has a strong gamey taste

explanation.surface: Choosing between chicken leg and breast portions, with a pungent flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: High meat, especially game, has been hung until its flavour is very strong.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh is the upper section of the leg, between hip and knee, so it is part of a leg.

clue.text: Shoot mad miner in entrance

indicators.note: mad means crazed, so the letters of the word next to it go wild
in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a gate is a way in

explanation.surface: An order to gun down a crazed miner at the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' looks like a command to fire a gun; it is the verb for a seed sprouting.
explanation.definitionFit: To germinate is to begin growing and put out a shoot, as a seed does.

clue.text: Go round with books in class

indicators.note: in tells us the first piece sits inside the second

blocks.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
a first-rate thing is in the first class

explanation.surface: Passing textbooks round a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn about an axis, going round in a circle.

clue.text: Pious tear always covered up

indicators.note: something covered up is wrapped inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: ever means at all times
a rent is a rip in cloth

explanation.surface: A devout person always hiding their tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' suggests weeping, but here it rhymes with 'bear': a rip, like a rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means showing deep respect, especially religious devotion, so it suits a pious person.
